15867.note: Port Canaveral seafood deck and tiki bar on the harbor.

15871.note: Oyster bar in The Cove at Port Canaveral, overlooking the cruise and fishing harbor.
15871.fn: Space Coast tourism listing says it was founded in 1993.

16087.note: Fish-camp-themed grill a block north of the Cocoa Beach Pier serving "swamp food" and fried seafood.

16156.note: Old Florida dive on the Indian River Lagoon at Channel Marker 35 with boat docking and a "hook 'em, we'll cook 'em" policy for your own catch.

16176.note: Long-running beachside raw bar on A1A in Indialantic.
16176.fn: Space Coast tourism listing says it has served the area since 1981; continuity at this address not confirmed.

16236.note: Small Malabar spot on US 1 serving Puerto Rican food.

16248.note: Downtown Melbourne Cuban restaurant started by a Cuban pilot who defected, with pre-Castro Havana decor, conga-drum counter stools and live music on weekends.

16359.fn: Camp Holly says it dates to the early 1920s as Brevard County's first fish camp; the restaurant's own opening year was not confirmed.

16533.note: Overwater seafood grill on the Indian River in Melbourne's Eau Gallie district.

16806.note: Merritt Island Cuban restaurant with a casual fine-dining take on traditional dishes.

17221.note: Titusville landmark for wild-caught Port Canaveral shrimp, broiled, steamed or fried, with its signature corn fritters.

17254.note: Family-owned Italian seafood grill and oyster bar on US 1 in Titusville.
17254.fn: The family business says it began in 1979 as a neighborhood pizzeria; the Titusville location's opening year was not confirmed.
